newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng seen ready to challenge 14,000.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng seen ready to challenge 14,000.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index looks set to challenge 14,000 points in the near term after storming to a record high on Wednesday, analysts said.
A surge by banking and property stocks and receding fears of higher interest rates powered the blue-chip index to its third-biggest point gain ever on Wednesday.
The Hang Seng jumped 472.78 points, or 3.56 percent, to close at 13,766.65, beating its previous record close of 13,530.95 on November 27 last year.
It posted an intra-day record of 13,771.54 points, overshooting the previous record of 13,744.30 on November 28.
"Basically, the underlying tone of the market remains very firm," said Abhijit Chakrabortti, senior strategist at Lehman Brothers. "We are literally on the doorstep of 14,000."

Analysts said the market had been trapped in a range of about 13,000 to 13,500 points since its last record high as investors feared a correction on Wall Street and the possibility of higher interest rates.

But benign U.S. consumer price data cheered U.S. investors on Tuesday, pushing the Dow industrial average up 53.11 points to 6,762.29, its fourth straight record close. The price of the 30-year U.S. long bond rose one full point to yield 6.77 percent.
"When you came in this morning and the bond market had had a rally, there was a lot of pent-up interest," said Richard Verin, head of equity trading at CS First Boston in Hong Kong.

"You really had two powerful things happening -- the interest rate scenario looks better and the property market is extremely strong. There were a lot of warrant issues recently that has led to buying of the underlying shares which has pushed it as well," he said.

Analysts said the Hong Kong government's first land auction of the year, held on Wednesday, boosted sentiment in the property sector. A 2,008 square metre site at Repulse Bay on the south side of Hong Kong island sold for HK$230 million (US$29.7 million) and a 5,080 square metre site in Tuen Mun in the New Territories fetched HK$258 million.
"The price which it (the auction) fetched was reasonably well above what the consensus expected," said Chakrabortti.
Brokers said funds from overseas had been flowing into Hong Kong on Wednesday. The day's turnover was HK$14.17 billion, the fifth-highest ever recorded by the Hong Kong stock exchange.
"When funds start coming in they won't suddenly stop," said Tam. "The index will go to 14,000 over the next two weeks because I think the market is on a huge rally."

Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc, which analysts said accounted for a good slice of the Hang Seng Index's rise on Wednesday, were expected to continue pushing higher ahead of the company's earnings announcement to be released on March 3.
The banking giant's shares surged HK$8.50 to HK$179 after earlier reaching an all-time high of HK$180.

"We think that even at this price level HSBC is seriously undervalued," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities. He added the stock could climb to HK$196 by the time the company's earnings are released.

"I think there is every chance 14,500 (on the Hang Seng) will be seen in the first quarter, particularly if you perceive that there is opportunity for the bank (HSBC) to trade close to HK$200 where a lot of analysts believe it is fair value," added Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities. ($1 = HK$7.74)
